segments.text: Most of the web was built for people clicking. Agents arrive and guess: they read PDFs, fill forms whose rules they can't see, and stop at fax numbers. WebMCP lets a site say exactly what an agent may do, but every site has to be retrofitted by hand. Overturn is the process that does it: analyze, find the gaps, recommend the tools, generate the code, and prove it with the person still in charge.

Paste a URL. Overturn Retrofit reads the site's forms, tables, documents and submission instructions. This is a health plan's member portal. Readiness: forty out of a hundred. Two blockers: the facts live inside PDFs, and the consequential step is fax or mail. Two gaps: the rules the decision cites aren't exposed, and support is phone-only. From that it recommends nine tools: reads for the list, the decision and the plan's criteria; a draft that renders as a proposal; a completeness check; and a submit gated behind a human click. Then it generates the register-tool code. And here is that plan, built.

The loop: analyze, recommend, generate, apply, verify. The rules are short. Reads are free. Writes are proposals the page renders. Consequential actions wait for a human click. Every call is logged on the page.
Before: on the legacy portal, an automation agent gets exactly as far as a person does. The letter, the six-page form, the fax number. It stalls.

After: same portal, same account, with the recommended tools. The agent reads the structured denial and the plan's five criteria, opens the appeal, and drafts one argument per criterion citing Maya's records. The draft lands on the page, labelled and editable. Attaching records is Maya's job; she attaches three and rewrites one argument herself. The agent notices, re-checks, five of five, and proposes expedited review. Then it asks to submit. It cannot submit; it can only ask. Maya signs. Case number, seventy-two-hour clock, and the tool surface changes: drafting tools out, status tools in.

Why it matters. Every site owner faces this retrofit; Overturn turns a guess into a plan. In healthcare the plan side is being made machine-readable by law: CMS rule 0057-F, seven-day decisions now, a structured API by 2027. And the payoff counts: three point six million winnable denials a year go unfiled. Each becomes one sitting. The same shape repeats in every claim-like dispute.
Overturn. Analyze any site, retrofit it for agents, keep the person in charge. Built for the WebMCP Challenge by Prathap, Rajani and Chitral. Open source, MIT.
